rationale: community: Strong modularity (0.5194) and high homophily (0.7492) indicate well-defined community structure; banned tolokers likely deviate from their community's behavioral norms. p99-p50 gap (0.5046) shows clear tail separation. attr_struct_mismatch: Strongest tail separation (p99-p50 gap 0.6003); cross-modal divergence between attribute-space and structure-based rankings captures nodes where collaboration patterns mismatch their profile. local_affinity: High homophily (0.7492) ensures neighbors are meaningful; normalized cosine similarity is robust to attribute scale variation. p99-p50 gap (0.4987) shows good separation. Together these provide complementary evidence: community fit, attribute-structure divergence, and neighbor agreement.

Banned workers are expected to be structurally and behaviorally distinct. The graph exhibits high homophily (0.7492), strong communities (modularity=0.5194, 26 communities), and high clustering (0.5329), making neighbour- and community-relative anomalies detectable. attr_struct_mismatch leads with the strongest tail (p99=0.9141 vs p50=0.3138), capturing workers whose attribute profile and structural position diverge—a key signature of anomalies. homophily_violation (p99=0.841) directly flags workers whose attributes mismatch their neighbours, expected in a high-homophily graph where deviations are rare. community (p99=0.7341) complements with community-aware measurement, detecting workers that don't fit their detected group's centroid. Together these three views span cross-modal agreement, neighbour-relative attributes, and community structure—complementary frames on a graph with clear structural organization. density is collapsed (p50=p90=p95=0), spectral is indirect, conformity's inverted sign and tight distribution (p99/p50≈1.11) contradict the task, and local_affinity is redundant with homophily_violation.

Banned tolokers are expected to deviate structurally and behaviorally from their project communities. homophily_violation has a strong separated tail (p99=0.841 vs p50=0.3628) and directly captures feature divergence from neighbors—banned workers should mismatch their coworkers. attr_struct_mismatch has the strongest signal overall (p99=0.9141 vs p50=0.3138), measuring cross-modal disagreement between attribute-space and structure-based rankings; this catches workers whose profile and structural role diverge, a hallmark of anomalous behavior. community builds on the strong community structure (modularity=0.5194, homophily=0.7492, num_communities=26) with a separated tail (p99=0.7341 vs p50=0.2295), detecting workers who don't fit their project community's attribute centroid. Together these three provide complementary views: neighbor-relative, community-relative, and cross-modal, all with clean signal separation despite the moderately high avg_degree=88.28.

The edge mechanism here is co-participation on a task, not attribute similarity, and avg_degree = 88.28 with density = 0.015 puts every node's neighbourhood close to the global mean. That is exactly the stated degeneration condition for local_affinity, homophily_violation and (by inheritance of its neighbour-relative half) attr_struct_mismatch, so their wide landmarker tails (homophily_violation p99 0.841 vs p50 0.363, attr_struct_mismatch p99 0.914 vs p50 0.314) are most likely reading degree and raw attribute scale rather than deviant workers; I drop all three despite their spread. A ban is handed out inside a project, so the right reference frame is a worker against the peers they co-worked with, and Louvain gives a usable one: modularity = 0.519 with homophily = 0.749 over 26 communities is a genuine partition (well above the ~0.3 floor) and the communities are small enough that their centroids are not the global mean. The community landmarker backs this with a real separated tail (p50 0.230, p90 0.544, p99 0.734). That is the primary view. Reconstruction is the second, deliberately in a different frame: feature_dim = 10 with feature_sparsity = 0.48 is dense and low-dimensional, far from the 'model fits the zeros' failure, and while the large neighbourhoods do push its error toward 'distance from the global attribute mean', that degradation is benign for this task, because banned tolokers are defined by extreme profile and task-performance statistics rather than by disagreeing with whoever happened to share a task with them. one_class adds the third, non-redundant frame: a single global boundary is the direct encoding of 'this worker sits outside the normal performance envelope', judged against the bulk rather than against neighbours or community peers; its GCN smoothing makes it structure-aware where density is purely attribute-side, and its only risk is embedding collapse, which is visible at fusion time. Excluded: density is dead on the evidence (p50 = p90 = p95 = 0, p99 = 0.048, no tail at all) since LOF on 10 raw mixed-scale attributes with feature_dup_rate = 0.489 puts most nodes inside duplicate-saturated neighbourhoods; conformity has the flattest shape of any landmarker (p99 0.969 vs p50 0.870, a 0.10 gap against ~0.5 for the others) and carries an inverted sign, so a wrong call is actively anti-correlated, a bad trade for a view with no separated tail; spectral degenerates precisely on dense graphs where one-hop smoothing removes almost nothing, and at 11758 nodes it falls back to that residual variant; adversarial and contrastive would add global attribute-robustness views redundant with one_class and reconstruction, and contrastive is further weakened by feature_dup_rate = 0.489, where dropout changes little.

The task is peer deviation: a banned toloker is a worker whose profile and performance statistics look wrong next to the people who worked on the same tasks, so cohort-relative and global-outlier frames are both relevant, and the evidence says which implementations survive here. Community fits best: modularity 0.5194 with 26 communities over 11758 nodes and homophily 0.7492 mean the Louvain partition is real and the cohorts are roughly project sized (about 450 nodes), far from the 'few very large communities' failure, and its landmarker carries a genuine tail (p50 0.2295 to p99 0.7341). This is the cohort-of-co-workers comparison the practitioner actually wants. Reconstruction adds an attribute-model view over only 10 attributes with moderate sparsity (0.4803), so the decoder cannot cheat by fitting zeros; avg_degree 88.28 does push it toward ranking nodes by distance from a heavily smoothed attribute signal, but for performance statistics that degraded mode still surfaces workers with extreme approval/rejection profiles rather than becoming noise. One_class supplies the only genuinely global frame that is not compromised: it judges each node against the bulk instead of against a neighbour average, so it is immune to the high-degree averaging problem, and with feature_dim 10 the embedding has little room to be dominated by sparse noise (its known collapse mode is the accepted risk, and it is placed third for that reason). Local_affinity is kept last as the one-hop cohort view at a different granularity from community: cosine on L2-normalised rows reads profile shape rather than magnitude, and clustering_coeff 0.5329 with homophily 0.7492 means a neighbourhood is a cohesive task cohort, not a random sample of the graph, which partly offsets the resolution loss expected at avg_degree 88.28. Excluded: density, whose landmarker is collapsed (p50, p90 and p95 all exactly 0, p99 0.0476), unsurprising with feature_dup_rate 0.489 putting many identical rows at distance zero; homophily_violation and attr_struct_mismatch, the first redundant with local_affinity by its own definition and the second inheriting both that neighbour-relative degradation and the dead attribute-space kNN half; spectral, since with n above 3000 and avg_degree 88.28 one-hop smoothing on a single attribute norm removes almost nothing; adversarial, a saturation risk on 10 raw unnormalised statistics; and conformity, whose landmarker has no separated tail (p50 0.8696 against p99 0.9686, mass piled at the top) and whose inverted sign makes it actively anti-correlated when wrong, which is the likely case here since bans follow extreme performance statistics rather than template-minimal profiles.

The decisive fact is avg_degree = 88.28 with density = 0.015: every neighbour-relative frame collapses here, because a mean over ~88 neighbours is already the global mean. That rules out local_affinity, homophily_violation and attr_struct_mismatch (which inherits the neighbour-relative half). The edge semantics make this worse rather than better: an edge means 'worked on the same task', a co-participation mechanism with no reason to align with a worker's profile or performance statistics, so neighbour disagreement is the normal state for honest tolokers, not the anomalous one. Their landmarkers have spread (local_affinity p99 0.697 vs p50 0.198, attr_struct_mismatch p99 0.914 vs p50 0.314) but a landmarker cannot show sign or cause, and here the mechanism that produces that spread is degree and task-sharing structure, not bans. Ban evidence lives in the 10 attributes (profile and task performance statistics), so the views worth running are the ones whose reference frame is global or community-scale. reconstruction leads: at degree 88 the decoder reconstructs every node from a nearly common smoothed signal, so the error degenerates into a ranking by distance from the global attribute mean, and that degenerate output is exactly the target signal here, a worker whose performance statistics sit far from the population is the one who gets banned. feature_sparsity 0.48 is moderate, so the fit-the-zeros failure is only partial. community is second on domain grounds: the ban is defined per project, 13 projects were sampled, and Louvain recovers 26 communities at modularity 0.5194 with homophily 0.749, a genuinely strong partition of roughly 450 nodes each, so the community centroid is a real project-peer reference and is not the global mean; scoring a worker against their own project cohort and normalising by that cohort's spread matches 'banned in one of the projects' better than any whole-graph comparison, and its landmarker separates (p50 0.230, p90 0.544, p99 0.734). one_class adds the third distinct frame, a single global boundary in a learned embedding, which is the one view that is structurally immune to the high-degree problem because it never averages over neighbours; it covers the case where atypicality is a joint pattern across the 10 attributes rather than a large reconstruction residual, at the known risk of embedding collapse, in which case its near-constant scores simply add nothing to the fusion. Rejected on evidence: density is flat (p90 = p95 = 0.0, mean 0.0023), it separates only a microscopic tail and cannot rank the bulk, even though 10 dense dimensions would normally suit LOF; conformity is the most dangerous option, feature_dup_rate 0.489 passes its gate but its landmarker is piled at the top with a compressed tail (p50 0.870, p99 0.969, a gap of 0.099), and banned workers are identified by deviant performance statistics, not by hiding behind minimal profiles, so an inverted-sign view that is wrong is actively anti-correlated; spectral sees only the attribute norm and one-hop smoothing removes almost nothing at this density; contrastive is undercut by dup_rate 0.489 and 48% zeros, dropout on a redundant 10-dim row changes little; adversarial gives a fourth global view with a saturation failure mode and no landmarker to check it, so it is left out in favour of three views with distinct, non-redundant reference frames.

All have strong upper-tail separation in scores.

The graph has extreme average degree (736.5) and high density (0.123), which degenerates neighbor-relative methods: local_affinity and homophily_violation both lose resolution as neighbor averages converge to the global mean. The landmarker evidence strongly favors cross-modal detection: attr_struct_mismatch shows the highest signal (mean=0.3697, p99=0.9158), directly capturing divergence between attribute-based and structure-based views—precisely the signature of fraudsters who differ from their neighbors in behavior despite sharing products/ratings. Contrastive embedding robustness avoids neighbor-averaging by operating on a globally trained embedding space and measuring stability under attribute dropout; it is robust to high-degree graphs. One_class provides complementary global boundary detection independent of local neighborhoods, useful for finding globally anomalous fraudsters. Weak community structure (modularity=0.25) rules out the community paradigm; low density signal in LOF (mean=0.0114) rules out density; reconstruction degenerates under large neighborhoods.

The very high average degree (736.5) makes neighbor-relative paradigms degenerate—neighbor averages approach the global mean, eroding resolution. This eliminates local_affinity, homophily_violation, and community (modularity=0.2485 is too weak). attr_struct_mismatch shows the strongest landmarker tail separation (p95=0.8098, p99=0.9158), indicating fraudsters violate both attribute and structural patterns in detectable ways despite degeneration. Complement this cross-modal view with two global embedding-based paradigms unaffected by high degree: contrastive (embedding stability under attribute dropout, captures nodes fragile to perturbation) and one_class (distance from bulk in learned space, identifies global outliers). This trimodal strategy avoids redundancy—disagreement measurement + embedding robustness + center distance—and sidesteps the high-degree trap that would nullify purely neighbor-relative evidence.

attr_struct_mismatch (p95=0.81) and local_affinity (p95=0.80) both show strong separation despite avg_degree=736.5 where neighborhood methods typically degenerate, indicating the multi-relation edges create genuine attribute divergence. attr_struct_mismatch captures cross-modal divergence between attribute-space and structure-based rankings (strongest signal), critical for fraud detection where fraudsters coordinate by product/rating/similarity relations but diverge in attributes like helpful votes. local_affinity detects local neighbor disagreement (cosine on normalized attributes), complementing the cross-modal view. one_class provides orthogonal global embedding view via Deep SVDD, detecting anomalies far from the normal population center. Weak community structure (modularity=0.2485 < 0.3) makes community-based methods unreliable. Together these three target complementary mechanisms: cross-modal divergence, local disagreement, and global outlier detection.

The decisive fact in this profile is the density: 8.8M directed edge entries over 11,944 nodes gives density 0.1233 and avg_degree 736.5, so every node's neighbourhood already covers a large share of the graph. Every neighbour-relative frame is therefore measuring the global mean twice and subtracting: local_affinity, homophily_violation and attr_struct_mismatch all name large average degree as their degeneration condition, and the landmarkers confirm it. local_affinity sits at mean 0.5035 with p50 0.5288, a near-symmetric spread with no separated upper tail, which is the signature of a comparison with no resolution left rather than of a mechanism that is present. homophily_violation (p50 0.1428, p90 0.2318) is a compressed body with a thin tail from the degree extremes. attr_struct_mismatch does show a wide spread (p90 0.7402), but half of it is the homophily-violation ranking, so the apparent separation is the difference between a meaningful attribute ranking and a degenerate structural one, which is noise by its own stated failure mode. reconstruction is disqualified for the same reason: a GCN decoder aggregating over 736 neighbours reconstructs every node from nearly the same smoothed signal. community is disqualified independently: modularity 0.2485 is below the ~0.3 threshold and Louvain found only 7 communities over 11,944 nodes, so each centroid is close to the global mean and the per-community spread normalisation removes the remainder. The reported homophily of 0.4967 is same-community edge fraction, not attribute agreement, so it carries no evidence for a neighbour-relative view here. What survives is exactly the set of globally-framed and edge-free views, and that matches the domain. Fraud here is defined at the user level by helpful-vote ratio, and the 25 handcrafted per-user features are review-behaviour summaries (rating patterns, text and timing statistics), so a fraudulent user is one whose behavioural profile sits outside the bulk of ordinary reviewers. The three merged relations (same product, same star rating within a week, top 5% text similarity) are camouflage-prone co-occurrence links, which is precisely why fraudsters are not isolated from normal neighbours and why the signal has to be read against the population rather than against neighbours. one_class is the primary view: its single moving centre judges a node against the bulk of all nodes, and its GCN smoothing over the dense graph is a mild regulariser rather than the fatal blur it is for a reconstruction target. Its known risk is embedding collapse, which is why I pair it with a view that cannot share that failure. density is that pair: LOF with 20 neighbours on the raw 25-dimensional attribute rows, reading no edges at all, so the graph's density cannot touch it. Its degeneration condition (high-dimensional or binary sparse attributes) does not hold, since feature_dim is only 25 and feature_sparsity is 0.4156 with feature_dup_rate 0.1762, far from template-dominated. Its landmarker is the heavy-tailed shape expected of a genuine minority outlier set (p50 0.0076, p99 0.0602). adversarial is the third and most tentative: it is the only remaining view with a global reference frame that reads structure and attributes jointly, so it can catch fraudsters whose individual rows look ordinary but whose attribute-plus-neighbourhood combination does not, which is the standard camouflage case on this platform. I rank it last because its noise discriminator can saturate into a narrow band on handcrafted features of mixed scale, and I would down-weight it if its output distribution comes back collapsed. I deliberately stop at three: the useful evidence here comes from one reference frame (global or attribute-space), and adding the neighbour-relative views back would not add a complementary angle, it would average a strong global signal against high-degree noise and pull the composition toward chance.

avg_degree = 736.5 with density = 0.1233 puts this graph squarely in the regime each neighbour-relative paradigm names as its own failure: the neighbour average converges to the global mean, so local_affinity, homophily_violation and attr_struct_mismatch (which inherits the neighbour-relative half of its rank difference) all lose resolution. The landmarkers agree rather than contradict this. local_affinity is a broad, nearly symmetric band (mean 0.5035, p50 0.5288) whose p99 is only 1.67x its median, which is spread without a separated upper tail, and attr_struct_mismatch is close to uniform by construction. modularity = 0.2485 sits below the 0.3 threshold with only 7 communities over 11944 nodes, so a Louvain centroid is essentially the global mean and dividing by the community spread removes what little is left; community is out despite its p99 of 0.404. spectral falls back to the one-hop residual above 3000 nodes, and at degree 736 one-hop smoothing removes almost nothing, on top of seeing only attribute magnitude. What survives is the global and attribute-space frames, which is also what the domain argues for: the three merged relations (same product, same star rating within a week, top 5% TF-IDF similarity) attach fraudulent reviewers to large numbers of benign users by construction, so disagreement with neighbours is camouflaged away, and the practitioner's target (share of helpful votes) is a per-user behavioural property, not a relational one. The discriminative content is in the 25 handcrafted per-user features themselves. one_class leads: a single global centre judges each node against the bulk of all nodes rather than against its neighbours, which is the one frame the high degree does not break, and 'outside the normal boundary in behavioural space' is the right shape for fraudulent accounts. Its stated risk is embedding collapse, which is why it is not run alone. reconstruction is kept with its degeneration read as an asset here: at this degree the decoder does rank nodes by distance from the global attribute mean, and over 25 hand-engineered fraud-relevant statistics that ranking is aligned with the target instead of orthogonal to it, while feature_sparsity = 0.4156 is moderate enough that the zero-fitting failure does not apply. It gives the trained, graph-aware version of the same global judgement. density contributes the only edge-free view: LOF reads raw attribute rows and never touches the edge list, so the density that disables everything else cannot reach it, and feature_dim = 25 is low enough that nearest-neighbour distances do not concentrate. It is placed third because feature_dup_rate = 0.1762 makes LOF unstable on byte-identical rows and its landmarker (mean 0.0114, p99 0.0602) indicates a few extreme points rather than a broad anomalous population, so it serves as a complement and not as a lead. adversarial is left out: the 25 heterogeneously scaled handcrafted statistics are exactly the case where fixed-variance Gaussian noise is trivially detectable on some columns and invisible on others, so discriminator saturation is the likely outcome.

This graph is extraordinarily dense: avg_degree 736.5 on only 11944 nodes, density 0.1233, max_degree 6991. At that degree every neighbour average converges to the global mean, which is the stated degeneration condition for local_affinity, homophily_violation, and (by inheritance of its neighbour-relative half) attr_struct_mismatch. Their landmarkers look alive (local_affinity mean 0.5035 with a smooth tail, attr_struct_mismatch p90 0.7402) but that shape is exactly what a converged neighbour average produces, so the spread is a scale artifact rather than evidence of the mechanism. Reconstruction fails for the same reason its own note gives: a GCN decoder aggregating over ~736 neighbours reconstructs every node from nearly the same smoothed signal and ends up ranking distance from the global attribute mean. Community-relative views are also out: modularity 0.2485 is below the ~0.3 threshold and Louvain finds only 7 communities over 11944 nodes, so each centroid sits near the global mean and the per-community spread normalisation removes the remainder (community landmarker mean 0.0663, p50 0.0436, consistent with a near-degenerate statistic). Spectral is excluded twice over: it sees only the attribute norm, and at this density one-hop smoothing removes almost nothing. What survives is the global reference frame. The fraud definition here is a property of the user, not of who the user is adjacent to: helpful-vote ratio below 20% describes an account whose 25 handcrafted behavioural features sit outside the bulk of legitimate reviewers, and the three merged relations (U-P-U, U-S-U, U-V-U) are precisely the camouflage channels that let such an account share neighbourhoods with benign users. one_class leads because a single Deep SVDD centre judges a node against the whole population rather than against neighbours it has deliberately blended into, which is the only frame the density does not erase; the GCN smoothing that hurts the reconstruction and affinity views is harmless here because the distance is taken against a global centre afterwards. density is the strongest complement because it reads no edges at all, so the 736-degree problem cannot touch it, and its stated failure mode does not apply: feature_dim is 25, low enough that LOF distances do not concentrate, and feature_sparsity 0.4156 means the rows are dense real-valued handcrafted statistics rather than binary sparse vectors. contrastive supplies a third view in a globally trained embedding space; with only 25 dimensions each dropped entry perturbs a large share of the row, and feature_dup_rate 0.1762 leaves most rows distinct, so the attribute-redundancy failure is limited. The three are complementary by construction: one global embedding boundary that uses the edges, one attribute-space view that ignores them, and one stability view, with no neighbour-relative or community-relative member to dilute them.
